track.title: The toolchain
track.blurb: What `python app.py` actually does between you pressing enter and the program starting: bytecode, `__pycache__`, and why Python has no compile step but definitely has a compiler.

track.title: Names and objects
track.blurb: Python has no variables. `a = b` binds a second name to one object, and almost every surprising bug in this book begins by forgetting that.

track.title: Mutability and aliasing
track.blurb: The list that changed when you were not looking. Aliasing, shallow copies, and the default argument that is created once and kept for the life of the process.

track.title: The data model
track.blurb: Everything is an object and every operator is a method call. Duck typing stated precisely enough that you can predict what will break.

track.title: Equality, hashing, truthiness
track.blurb: The `__eq__` and `__hash__` contract, why a mutable dict key is a bug lying in wait, and what `if x:` actually calls.

track.title: Expressions and statements
track.blurb: What counts as an expression, what the walrus is for, and the evaluation order you have been assuming without ever checking.

track.title: Control flow
track.blurb: `for`/`else`, the loop that finished versus the loop that broke, and `match` — the newest control structure in the language and the least used.

track.title: Functions
track.blurb: Positional-only, keyword-only, `*args`, `**kwargs`, and the single most important fact about defaults: when they are evaluated.

track.title: Scope and closures
track.blurb: LEGB, the closure that captured a variable rather than a value, and why every function you made in that loop returned the same answer.

track.title: Exceptions
track.blurb: A recoverable error is something you catch; a bug is a traceback. `raise ... from`, EAFP over LBYL, and the exception groups 3.11 added.

track.title: Sequences and slicing
track.blurb: A slice is an object. Negative steps, slice assignment, and why `a[:]` copies but `a[:] = b` does not.

track.title: Strings, bytes and encoding
track.blurb: `str` is not `bytes`, and the difference will find you at a file boundary. Encodings, the format spec mini-language, and `!r`.

track.title: Dicts and sets
track.blurb: Hashing, the insertion order that became a language guarantee in 3.7, views, and the shape `setdefault` and `defaultdict` exist to fill.

track.title: Comprehensions and collections
track.blurb: A comprehension is a compiled construct with its own scope, not sugar for a loop. Plus the five `collections` types actually worth knowing.

track.title: Sorting and ordering
track.blurb: Key functions, why stability matters more than you expect, and the two stdlib modules that replace half the sorting code you would write.

track.title: The iterator protocol
track.blurb: `__iter__` and `__next__`, exhaustion, and the reason `for` works on things that are not sequences at all.

track.title: Generators
track.blurb: `yield` turns a function into a resumable object. Lazy pipelines, `send`, `throw`, and `yield from`.

track.title: itertools and functools
track.blurb: Seventy building blocks that compose, `cache` and `singledispatch`, and an honest verdict on `map`, `filter` and `reduce`.

track.title: Classes
track.blurb: `__new__` versus `__init__`, what a method actually is, and the class attribute that everyone mutates by accident exactly once.

track.title: Attribute access
track.blurb: `__dict__`, `__getattr__` versus `__getattribute__`, `__slots__`, and `property` as the first descriptor you ever meet.

track.title: Descriptors
track.blurb: The mechanism underneath `property`, methods, `classmethod` and `staticmethod`. One protocol explains all four, and this is the unit where the language clicks.

track.title: Inheritance and the MRO
track.blurb: C3 linearisation, what `super()` is really doing (not what you think), and the narrow case where multiple inheritance is the right call.

track.title: Dunder protocols
track.blurb: Operator overloading, `__repr__` versus `__str__`, what `with` compiles to, and a container you can implement in four methods.

track.title: Modern data modelling
track.blurb: `dataclass`, `NamedTuple` and `Enum`, and the precise point at which `attrs` and `pydantic` start earning their dependency.

track.title: Type hints
track.blurb: Annotations are runtime metadata, not enforcement. Generics, `TypeVar`, `Literal`, `TypedDict`, and `Protocol` — structural typing, finally.

track.title: Type checking in practice
track.blurb: mypy's strictness dials, the five errors you will actually hit, how to type a codebase that has none, and the point where types stop paying.

track.title: Decorators
track.blurb: A decorator is a function that takes a function. `functools.wraps`, parameters, and why the ones in real libraries look nothing like the tutorial ones.

track.title: Metaclasses and __init_subclass__
track.blurb: `type` is a callable that makes classes. When a metaclass is genuinely right (rarely) and why `__init_subclass__` usually beats reaching for one.

track.title: Introspection and the AST
track.blurb: `inspect`, `dis` and `ast`. Read your own bytecode, then write a transformer that rewrites source before it ever runs.

track.title: Modules, packages, imports
track.blurb: The import system in full: `sys.path`, packages, relative imports, and the circular import you can finally diagnose instead of shuffling.

track.title: Packaging and environments
track.blurb: `pyproject.toml`, `uv`, and shipping a wheel. From a folder of scripts to something a stranger can install by name.

track.title: Testing
track.blurb: pytest for real: fixtures, `parametrize`, honest mocking, and property-based tests that find the input you would never have thought of.

track.title: Tooling and practice
track.blurb: ruff, mypy and pre-commit as one pipeline, `logging` instead of `print`, and the handful of practices that survive contact with a team.

track.title: Concurrency models
track.blurb: The GIL, described accurately for once, including the free-threaded build. Threads, processes and async, and which one your problem actually needs.

track.title: async and await
track.blurb: A coroutine does nothing until something awaits it. The event loop, `TaskGroup`, and why one blocking call stalls the entire program.

track.title: Performance
track.blurb: Profile first, always. `cProfile`, `timeit`, the algorithmic win versus the micro one, and where the C boundary changes every rule.

track.title: Memory and the runtime
track.blurb: Reference counting plus a cycle collector. Weak references, why `__del__` is a trap, and the reason `getsizeof` lies to you.

track.title: The ecosystem, mapped
track.blurb: A map, not a tutorial: the stdlib modules you will really use and the dozen packages worth knowing, each with the case where it is the wrong answer.

track.title: Reading the traceback
track.blurb: Every other unit teaches a topic. This one teaches reading the traceback, which is what makes the next error survivable — including errors this book never covers.

projects.title: A Bloom filter
projects.blurb: A set that answers "definitely not" or "probably yes" in constant space, built on a bit array and k hashes, with the false positive rate measured against the formula.

projects.title: An LRU cache
projects.blurb: A dict and a doubly linked list, O(1) on both ends, then raced against `functools.lru_cache` to find out what the standard library is doing differently.

projects.title: A retry library
projects.blurb: Decorators with parameters, exponential backoff with jitter, and the exception-filtering predicate that turns a toy into something you would actually deploy.

projects.title: A regex engine
projects.blurb: Parse a pattern into a tree and walk it with a backtracking matcher, then find the pattern that makes your own engine take exponential time.

projects.title: An n-gram language model
projects.blurb: Count the contexts, smooth the counts so unseen words do not get probability zero, sample from the distribution, and read the text it writes back at you.

projects.title: micrograd
projects.blurb: A `Value` that remembers how it was computed, a backward pass over the graph, an MLP built from it, and a loss curve that actually falls.

projects.title: A BPE tokenizer
projects.blurb: The algorithm GPT and Llama really use: merge the commonest byte pair, over and over, until text is integers and the round trip is exact.

projects.title: A JSON parser
projects.blurb: A tokenizer and a recursive descent parser that reads a real document and, when it fails, names the exact character it failed on.

projects.title: A test framework
projects.blurb: Rebuild the useful third of pytest: collection, fixtures with teardown, and assertion rewriting through the `ast` module so a bare `assert` explains itself.

projects.title: An ORM
projects.blurb: Descriptors for the fields, a metaclass for the table, and generated SQL. After this, Django and SQLAlchemy stop being magic and start being code.

projects.title: An async crawler
projects.blurb: `asyncio` under load: a worker pool, a rate limiter, `TaskGroup` for structured concurrency, and backpressure so the queue cannot eat your memory.

projects.title: A key-value store
projects.blurb: An append-only write-ahead log, an in-memory index, compaction, and a crash in the middle of a write that the store recovers from.

projects.title: A CLI, shipped
projects.blurb: From `__main__.py` to a wheel on an index: argument parsing, entry points, `pyproject.toml`, a test matrix, and a version someone else can install.

projects.title: A web framework
projects.blurb: ASGI from the specification up: routing, middleware as a callable chain, request and response objects, and dependency injection in about forty lines.

projects.title: Build a GPT
projects.blurb: Tokenizer to embeddings to attention to a training loop to sampling. Consumes the BPE tokenizer and micrograd you already built, and ends with a model writing text.
